---
title: "Championships: NBA and WNBA eras"
---

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Why the time windows differ
- **NBA section:** every NBA season we have, **2003-04 to 2025-26** (23 seasons, 23 champions).
- **WNBA section:** every WNBA season we have, **2009 to 2026** (18 seasons, 18 champions).
- **NBA vs WNBA comparison:** only the **shared window, 2009 to 2026**, so differences between the leagues are not
  differences between years.
- **Models that learn from champions use all of each league's seasons.** There is only one champion per season, so a
  10-season window would leave just 10 champions to learn from, too few to test a title model. More seasons also
  give the era-drift results their meaning (e.g. the NBA's mid-2000s defense-led champions).
- Some measurements start later in both leagues (drive and pull-up tags: NBA 2017-18, WNBA 2019) and are used only where they exist.
- **Shot zones are calibrated by season.** ESPN's recorded shot positions drift between eras, most visibly in the
  WNBA's 2020 bubble season, so the rim zone is anchored to where layups are recorded each season (Data page).
:::

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from _viz import read, md, show, LEAGUE, SERIES

ZONES = ["three", "rim", "paint / short mid", "long mid"]
z = read("step5_playoff_zone_by_season.csv")
r = read("step5_playoff_zone_resilience.csv").dropna(subset=["pps_change"])
ci = read("step5_champion_identity.csv")
cv = read("step5_champion_vs_league.csv")
ing = read("step5_champions_by_era.csv")
tcv = read("step5_title_cv.csv")
nn = read("step5_title_no_net_cv.csv")
prof = read("step5_league_profiles.csv")
yb = read("step5_wnba_years_behind.csv")
ERAS = {"NBA": ([2003, 2010, 2016, 2021, 2026], ["2004-10", "2011-16", "2017-21", "2022-26"]),
        "WNBA": ([2008, 2013, 2017, 2021, 2026], ["2009-13", "2014-17", "2018-21", "2022-26"])}
SHARED = ([2008, 2013, 2017, 2021, 2026], ["2009-13", "2014-17", "2018-21", "2022-26"])


def era(df, lg, bins=None):
    b, lab = bins or ERAS[lg]
    return pd.cut(df.season, b, labels=lab)


def zone_chart(lg):
    col = LEAGUE[lg]
    fig = go.Figure()
    for zone, c in zip(ZONES, SERIES):
        d = z[(z.league == lg) & (z.zone == zone)].sort_values("season")
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.season, y=d.pps_change, name=zone, mode="lines+markers", line=dict(color=c, width=2),
                        marker=dict(size=6, color=c), hovertemplate=f"{zone}: " + "%{y:+.3f}<extra></extra>")
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.update_layout(height=360, yaxis_title="playoff minus regular-season pts/shot", legend=dict(y=1.14))
    return fig


def zone_table(lg):
    d = r[r.league == lg].copy()
    d["avg change"] = d.pps_change.map(lambda x: f"{x:+.3f}")
    d["95% interval"] = [f"{lo:+.3f} to {hi:+.3f}" for lo, hi in zip(d.lo95, d.hi95)]
    d["seasons worse in playoffs"] = d.seasons_worse_in_playoffs.map(lambda x: f"{x:.0%}")
    return d[["zone", "seasons", "avg change", "95% interval", "seasons worse in playoffs"]].to_markdown(index=False)


def identity_chart(lg):
    d = ci[ci.league == lg]
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.off_edge, y=d.def_edge, mode="markers", showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=10, color=LEAGUE[lg], line=dict(width=2, color="#fcfcfb")),
                    customdata=d[["season", "team", "off_rank", "def_rank", "n_teams", "identity"]],
                    hovertemplate="%{customdata[0]} %{customdata[1]}<br>offense #%{customdata[2]:.0f}, defense #%{customdata[3]:.0f} of %{customdata[4]}<br>%{customdata[5]}<extra></extra>")
    for _, row in d[d.season >= 2022].iterrows():
        fig.add_annotation(x=row.off_edge, y=row.def_edge, text=f"{row.team} {row.season % 100:02d}", showarrow=False,
                           yshift=13, font=dict(size=11))
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#8a8984", width=1))
    fig.update_layout(height=400, hovermode="closest", xaxis_title="offense edge vs league (pts/100)",
                      yaxis_title="defense edge vs league (pts/100)")
    return fig


def champ_tables(lg):
    c = cv[cv.league == lg].copy()
    c["era"] = era(c, lg)
    cols = {"three_share_vs_league": "threes", "rim_share_vs_league": "rim", "mid_share_vs_league": "mid-range",
            "assisted_share_vs_league": "assisted makes"}
    g = c.groupby("era", observed=True)
    t = (g[list(cols)].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=cols)
    t.insert(0, "champions", g.size())
    shot = t.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False)
    i = ci[ci.league == lg].copy()
    i["era"] = era(i, lg)
    arch = [x for x in i.columns if x.startswith("arch_vs_league::")]
    g = i.groupby("era", observed=True)
    a = (g[arch].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=lambda x: x.split("::")[1])
    a.insert(0, "identity mix", g.identity.agg(lambda s: ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in s.value_counts().items())))
    return shot, a.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False)


def title_table(lg):
    a = tcv[tcv.league == lg][["model", "mean_prob_on_champion", "mean_loglik_champion"]]
    b = nn[(nn.league == lg) & ~nn.model.str.contains("reference")][["model", "mean_prob_on_champion", "mean_loglik_champion"]]
    t = pd.concat([a, b])
    t.columns = ["model", "avg prob. on champion", "log-lik (higher is better)"]
    return t.round(3).to_markdown(index=False)
```

```{python}
#| label: takeaways
nz = r[r.league == "NBA"].set_index("zone")
wz = r[r.league == "WNBA"]
w_any = ((wz.lo95 > 0) | (wz.hi95 < 0)).any()
last = yb[yb.wnba_season == yb.wnba_season.max()].set_index("feature")
three_now = prof[(prof.league == "WNBA")].set_index("season").three_share.iloc[-1]
c = cv[cv.season >= 2022].groupby("league")[["three_share_vs_league", "rim_share_vs_league"]].mean() * 100
md(f"""::: {{.callout-note appearance="simple"}}
## Takeaways
- **NBA playoffs punish threes and rim attempts.** Points per three fell in the playoffs in
  {nz.loc['three', 'seasons_worse_in_playoffs']:.0%} of {int(nz.loc['three', 'seasons'])} seasons ({nz.loc['three', 'pps_change']:+.3f} per shot);
  rim attempts in {nz.loc['rim', 'seasons_worse_in_playoffs']:.0%} ({nz.loc['rim', 'pps_change']:+.3f}). Mid-range shots held up best.
- **WNBA playoffs:** {'some zones show a reliable change' if w_any else 'no shot zone shows a reliable playoff change (every 95% interval includes zero)'}; with 8-12 playoff teams a year the sample is small.
- **The WNBA is about {last.loc['three_share', 'years_behind']:.0f} years behind the NBA on the three-point shift.** In {int(yb.wnba_season.max())},
  {three_now:.0%} of WNBA shots were threes.
- **Recent champions vs their own league (2022-26):** WNBA champions took {c.loc['WNBA', 'three_share_vs_league']:+.1f} points more of their shots from three and
  {c.loc['WNBA', 'rim_share_vs_league']:+.1f} at the rim; NBA champions {c.loc['NBA', 'three_share_vs_league']:+.1f} and {c.loc['NBA', 'rim_share_vs_league']:+.1f}.
:::""")
```

# NBA (2003-04 to 2025-26)

## NBA: which shots survive the playoffs?

Points per shot in the playoffs minus the regular season, by zone. Below zero = the shot got worse in the playoffs.

```{python}
show(zone_chart("NBA"))
md(zone_table("NBA"))
```

## NBA: champion identity

Each NBA champion's offense and defense relative to the league that season (points per 100 possessions; up and
right = better). *Offense-led* or *defense-led* when one side's edge beats the other's by 3 or more points.

```{python}
show(identity_chart("NBA"))
shot, arch = champ_tables("NBA")
md("**How NBA champions' shots differed from the league** (percentage points; + = more of that shot than the league)\n\n" + shot)
md("**NBA champions' archetype minutes minus the league average** (percentage points)\n\n" + arch)
e = ing[ing.league == "NBA"]
cols = {"C1_primary_scorer": "primary scorer", "C2_secondary_scorer": "secondary scorer", "C3_spacing_big": "spacing big",
        "C4_perimeter_d": "perimeter defender", "n_high_usage": "high-usage players"}
md("**Share of NBA champions with each ingredient** (loose definitions, meant to show drift)\n\n" +
   e[["era", *cols]].rename(columns=cols).round(2).to_markdown(index=False))
```

## NBA: picking champions

Forward-chained over NBA seasons: each season predicted from earlier NBA seasons only.

```{python}
md(title_table("NBA"))
```

# NBA vs WNBA (shared window, 2009 to 2026)

## Which era is each league in?

Share of regular-season shots from three and from mid-range, both leagues, 2009 onward.

```{python}
p = prof[prof.season >= 2009]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=("Share of shots from three", "Share of shots from mid-range"),
                    horizontal_spacing=0.1)
for j, f in enumerate(["three_share", "mid_share"], 1):
    for lg, col in LEAGUE.items():
        d = p[p.league == lg]
        fig.add_scatter(x=d.season, y=d[f], name=lg, legendgroup=lg, showlegend=(j == 1), mode="lines+markers",
                        line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=6, color=col),
                        hovertemplate=f"{lg}: " + "%{y:.1%}<extra></extra>", row=1, col=j)
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=".0%")
fig.update_layout(height=380, legend=dict(y=1.16))
show(fig)
```

**How many years behind the NBA is the WNBA?** For each WNBA season, the NBA season with the same share (NBA series
smoothed over 3 seasons; the NBA's full history is used as the yardstick). Blank where the WNBA value is outside the NBA's range.

```{python}
fig = go.Figure()
for f, nm, col in [("three_share", "three-point share", "#2a78d6"), ("mid_share", "mid-range share", "#eb6834")]:
    d = yb[yb.feature == f]
    fig.add_scatter(x=d.wnba_season, y=d.years_behind, name=nm, mode="lines+markers",
                    line=dict(color=col, width=2), marker=dict(size=8, color=col),
                    hovertemplate=nm + ": %{y:.1f} years behind<extra></extra>")
fig.update_layout(height=340, yaxis_title="years behind the NBA", xaxis_title="WNBA season", legend=dict(y=1.12))
show(fig)
```

## Champions vs their own league, side by side

Same eras for both leagues. Champion's shot share minus its league's, percentage points.

```{python}
c = cv[cv.season >= 2009].copy()
c["era"] = era(c, None, SHARED)
cols2 = {"three_share_vs_league": "threes", "rim_share_vs_league": "rim", "mid_share_vs_league": "mid-range"}
t = (c.groupby(["era", "league"], observed=True)[list(cols2)].mean() * 100).round(1).rename(columns=cols2).reset_index()
md(t.to_markdown(index=False))
i = ci[ci.season >= 2009].copy()
i["era"] = era(i, None, SHARED)
idm = i.groupby(["era", "league"], observed=True).identity.agg(lambda s: ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in s.value_counts().items())).unstack()
md("**Champion identity by era**\n\n" + idm.reset_index().to_markdown(index=False))
```

::: {.caveat}
Association, not causation. Each league is measured against itself; NBA and WNBA numbers are compared, never pooled.
:::
